Positively disrupting an industry that has not seen any innovation in over 50 years, Tekion has challenged the paradigm with the first and fastest cloud-native automotive platform that includes the revolutionary Automotive Retail Cloud (ARC) for retailers, Automotive Enterprise Cloud (AEC) for manufacturers and other large automotive enterprises and Automotive Partner Cloud (APC) for technology and industry partners. Tekion connects the entire spectrum of the automotive retail ecosystem through one seamless platform. The transformative platform uses cutting-edge technology, big data, machine learning, and AI to seamlessly bring together OEMs, retailers/dealers and consumers. With its highly configurable integration and greater customer engagement capabilities, Tekion is enabling the best automotive retail experiences ever. Tekion employs close to 3,000 people across North America, Asia and Europe.

 


JOB INTRODUCTION

The OEM Partnership team is expanding its engagement with automotive OEM clients and large dealer groups. As the volume and complexity of partnership opportunities grow, there is a critical need for a dedicated operations professional who can manage, track, and organize complex data sets, pipeline activity, and cross-functional deliverables. This role will serve as the operational backbone of the OEM Partnership team, ensuring that all client-facing activities are supported by accurate data, streamlined processes, and well-prepared materials. Without this role, the team risks losing visibility into key opportunities, experiencing delays in reporting, and being unable to scale efficiently. This position directly supports Tekion's strategic growth objectives within the OEM channel.





KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Manage and maintain OEM partnership pipeline data within Salesforce, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timely updates across all stages of the opportunity lifecycle.

 - Track, organize, and analyze complex data sets related to OEM partner engagements, dealer group activity, and market opportunities to provide actionable insights to leadership.

 - Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and tracking tools in Salesforce and Excel to monitor key performance indicators, deal progress, and team activity.

 - Prepare high-quality PowerPoint presentations, executive summaries, and briefing materials for OEM client meetings, quarterly business reviews, and internal leadership updates.

 - Coordinate cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success teams to ensure alignment on OEM partnership initiatives and deliverables.

 - Support the SVP of OEM Partnership with meeting preparation, follow-up action tracking, and operational cadence management.

 - Identify process gaps and proactively recommend improvements to enhance team efficiency, data quality, and reporting capabilities.

 - Serve as a key point of contact for operational inquiries from OEM clients and large dealer groups, maintaining a professional and knowledgeable presence.

 - Assist in the coordination of limited travel engagements (less than 20%) for OEM client visits, industry events, and dealer group meetings.

 - Maintain organized records of all partnership agreements, communications, and key milestones.

 - Strong automotive industry knowledge, including familiarity with OEM structures, dealer networks, and franchise operations.

 - Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP, data modeling, complex formulas) and Microsoft PowerPoint (executive-level presentation design).

ABOUT CONDUIT HEALTH

Conduit Health is transforming one of the most outdated corners of post-acute care—getting essential medical equipment and supplies into patients' homes. We're the first vertically integrated, AI-powered platform to unite ordering, telehealth, prescriptions, insurance, and fulfillment into one seamless experience. In seconds, case managers and providers can say "yes" to patients who would otherwise wait weeks — while we handle every step behind the scenes.


THE ROLE

We're looking for a Strategy & Operations Manager, Insurance to to own and scale our insurance operations as we expand into new states and payers. You’ll lead the team that handles eligibility, benefits, prior authorization, and coverage, and you’ll design the systems that keep orders clean, moving, and compliant at scale.  This is detective work at the level of the whole operation. When orders stall, you look past the individual case to the pattern behind it, then you partner with product and engineering to fix it upstream.

You'll report to the Head of Operations and work closely with our RCM, fulfillment, and product teams.

This is a chance to build a core function at a high-growth startup and shape how it scales, while working hands on with industry leaders and driving impact across our patient population.



WHO YOU ARE

 - A builder: You've designed and scaled operations at a high-growth company, not just run them. You turn messy, recurring problems into systems, workflows, and tooling that hold up as volume grows.

 - A team leader: You've managed and developed people. You set clear expectations, coach your team, and raise the bar for how work gets done.

 - A product and engineering partner: You know how to translate an operational pattern into a clear problem for product and engineering, and you've shipped fixes together.

 - Payer-literate: You understand how Medicaid, Medicare, and commercial payers work, or you've learned a complex, regulated domain quickly and can do it again. You operate within HIPAA and billing regulations by default.

 - Data-driven: You define the metrics that matter, build the reporting to track them, and use it to spot problems before they become backlogs.

 - Mission-aligned: You care deeply about healthcare access and getting patients what they need without the wait.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own insurance operations: Be accountable for eligibility, benefits verification, prior authorization, coverage, and denials across our patient population and payer mix.

 - Lead and grow the team: Manage, coach, and develop the insurance team. Set priorities, define roles, and hire as we scale.

 - Scale into new states and payers: Design the operational playbook for each new market, from payer requirements and plan structures to the workflows the team relies on.

 - Diagnose patterns, not just cases: Analyze stalled orders, denials, and rejections to find the root causes behind them, then close the gaps that cause them.

 - Build with product and engineering: Partner on the roadmap for insurance tooling. Turn recurring investigations into automated, repeatable workflows.

 - Own the metrics: Define and track KPIs such as eligibility hit rate, auth turnaround, denial rate, and clean-order rate. Report insights and recommendations to leadership.

 - Build the operating system: Create and maintain the SOPs, documentation, and training that let the team move fast and stay compliant.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 6+ years in strategy and operations, business operations, or healthcare insurance operations, ideally at a high-growth health tech or tech company.

 - Experience managing and developing a team.

 - A track record of building systems and processes in partnership with product and engineering.

 - Strong analytical skills; comfort building reports and working with data (SQL a plus).

 - Experience building SOPs and improving processes in a regulated environment.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.



The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.



Operating Principles:

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

 1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

 2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

 3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

 4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.




AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.



That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:



 - Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

 - Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

 - Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

 - Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.



We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

Behind many of life’s most important transactions like buying a house, applying for a mortgage, getting a small business loan, or refinancing a credit card, is a network of credit relationships. Setpoint provides critical infrastructure for relationships between the world’s largest banks, credit funds and capital markets counterparties. Because when capital works together, ambition goes further.
 Strategy & Operations Associate, GTM 
 Location: New York, New York | Hybrid (Tuesdays/Thursdays)
 About the role 
 Behind many of life’s most important transactions like buying a house, applying for a mortgage, getting a small business loan, or refinancing a credit card, is a network of credit relationships. Setpoint provides critical infrastructure for relationships between the world’s largest banks, credit funds and capital markets counterparties. Because when capital works together, ambition goes further.
 We are looking for a Strategy & Operations Associate, GTM hire to join our team. This role sits at the intersection of sales, operations, and AI. Today, much of what happens in our deals lives in email threads, Slack channels, and call recordings, and only part of it reaches HubSpot through manual rep updates. You will build the company intelligence layer that captures all of it, and the AI agents on top of it that keep our CRM current, surface insights for leadership, and give reps their time back to sell.
 Who will love this job: 
- An AI builder – you reach for Claude, GPT, and automation tools first, and you have built workflows, agents, or internal tools that people use every day
- A systems thinker – you see the CRM, inboxes, Slack, and call recordings as one data set and want to connect them
- A data-driven strategist – you use metrics to shape sales process and go-to-market strategy, not only to report on them
- An owner – you find the manual, low-value work that slows reps down and remove it without being asked
- A strong collaborator – you work across sales, marketing, product, and finance, and can explain technical work to a non-technical audience
 What you’ll do: 
- Company Intelligence Layer - Design and build an always-on intelligence ecosystem that captures what happens across email, Slack, and call recordings and connects it to HubSpot, so the full history of every account and deal lives in one place instead of in reps' inboxes and memories
- AI Agents for the Sales Team - Build and maintain agents on top of that data that do work on reps' behalf: monitoring calls, updating projected close dates, deal stages, and product mix in HubSpot, flagging at-risk deals, and drafting follow-ups
- Systems & Data Integrity - Own HubSpot (our CRM) end to end. Move the CRM from rep-entered data to system-maintained data, with clear field definitions, automated hygiene, and an audit trail so leadership can trust what it sees
- Reporting & Forecasting - Partner with sales leadership on pipeline management, quarter-end close, and the forecast that feeds financial planning, executive, and board materials. Build dashboards and reports that give visibility into key sales metrics
- GTM Strategy & Analysis - Analyze performance across the sales process, pricing, product mix, and ideal customer profile, and turn the findings into recommendations for leadership
- Account Management - Manage account distribution so reps keep a healthy pipeline, equitable account assignments, and a balanced mix of core ICP and experimental accounts. Use AI-driven enrichment to fill account data gaps that support qualification
- Enablement & Cross-Functional Collaboration - Roll out new tools and processes to the sales team with clear guides and training, and work with marketing, finance, product, and implementation to keep systems and processes aligned
 You should have: 
- 4-6+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Strategy & Operations, or a related role (ex. Business Operations, GTM Strategy)
- Hands-on HubSpo

About the Role : 
 We're hiring an Events Associate to create WITHIN events people actually want to go to: 2 to 4 a month, for the brand leaders we'd love to know better.
 Most of these will be in-person in cities with lots of brands: New York, LA, San Francisco, Chicago, Miami, Atlanta and others. Some will be content-led (panels, roundtables, workshops), some will just be fun gatherings, and a few will be webinars. None of them will be a stuffy steakhouse dinner. The bar: a great venue, a real reason to be in the room, and guests who leave having met people worth knowing. Done right, those relationships grow into ongoing conversations with our team, and some into long-term partnerships.
 You'll own each event end to end: the concept, the guest list, the outreach to fill it, the run of show, the WITHIN team on site, and the follow-up. You'll also make our time at industry conferences count, from lining up on-site meetings around our CEO's talks to finding creative ways to get in front of the right people. You'll report to the Director of Partnerships on the Revenue team.
 Responsibilities include but are not limited to; 
 Concept and plan the events 
- Pitch and plan 2 to 4 events a month, mixing content-led sessions, social gatherings and the occasional webinar
- Scout venues people get excited about (new restaurants, galleries, rooftops, studios, private rooms), not hotel ballrooms
- Manage budgets, vendors, venues, catering, collateral, and logistics for every event
- Build a calendar that keeps us showing up regularly in our key markets
 Fill the room with the right people 
- Personally invite marketing and ecommerce leaders at the brands we want in the room, by email, LinkedIn and phone
- Build guest lists with our team so every room has the right mix of people
- Manage RSVPs, reminders, and confirmations to cut no-shows
 Make every event worth the trip 
- Design the night so networking happens naturally: intros, seating, small-group formats, and bring the right WITHIN people, briefed on who's coming
- Own the follow-up so conversations keep going after the night ends: who reaches out, when, and with what
- Keep track of how relationships develop from RSVP onward
 Test and improve, every time 
- Run at least one test at every event, like a new invite angle, reminder cadence, format, time slot or follow-up sequence
- Measure attendance, repeat guests and what happens after each event, and share what's working
- Kill what doesn't work and double down on what does
- Report back on what each event delivered so we know where to invest  
 Build the community 
- Grow a network of brand leaders, partners and friends of WITHIN in each city
 Requirements: 
- Taste. You know the cool spots in every city, and you throw events people actually want to go to, because the room and the conversation are both worth it
- Scrappy. When the venue double-books or the speaker cancels an hour out, you find a fix and the guests never notice
- Calm under pressure, always prepared. You're probably type A: run of show done, backups for the backups
- A natural host. You can work a room, make the right introductions and make every guest feel welcome
- 1 to 3 years in events, field marketing, partnerships, hospitality or a similar role (agency, startup or B2B a plus)
- You've planned and run events yourself, even small ones, and you sweat the details
- You're comfortable cold calling and reaching out to people you don't know yet, you get creative when email gets ignored, and you don't mind hearing no
- You like testing things, you look at the numbers, and you're honest about what didn't work
- Strong writing for invites, follow-ups and sponsor decks
- Organized enough to juggle several events in different cities at once
 Nice to Have: 
- Experience with HubSpot or Salesforce
- A network in DTC, ecommerce or consumer brands

Travel: travel to LA, San Francisco, Chicago, Miami, Atlanta and other major

World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization whose mission is to boldly engage the world’s greatest crises in partnership with the church. Are you a person of compassion? An advocate for justice? Someone who stands up for the rights of the vulnerable and speaks out for the marginalized, the exploited and the forgotten?  Do you believe in our calling as Christians to welcome the least of these and love our neighbor?
 
If you answered ‘yes’, to any of the above, World Relief, and millions of people around the world need you.
 
At this pivotal moment in time, we are rapidly expanding and growing our team to meet the increasing needs of our world. We are looking for people who want to use their gifts and talents to make a real and tangible difference in our world and the lives of the suffering.
 
If you’re looking for a purpose-driven career in which you can grow your talents, while also standing up for the rights of the vulnerable, we want you to join us today.
 
 
ORGANIZATION SUMMARY
World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization whose mission is to boldly engage the world’s greatest crises in partnership with the church. The organization was founded in the aftermath of World War II to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of war-torn Europe. Since then, for 80 years, across 100 countries, World Relief has partnered with local churches and communities to build a world where families thrive and communities flourish.
 
Today, organizational programming focuses on humanitarian and disaster response, community strengthening and resilience, and refugee & immigrant services and advocacy.


POSITION SUMMARY:
World Relief seeks a Portfolio Development Manager (PDM), Growth Offices, to support a portfolio of 10 small and midsize U.S. offices as they grow their private fundraising capacity and strengthen local engagement. As the primary liaison between the home office and this designated portfolio, the PDM partners closely with office leaders and local Advancement staff to build sustainable fundraising strategies, develop revenue-generating skills, and activate private revenue growth. In this role, you'll provide hands-on coaching and guidance across donor development, church partnerships, major donor fundraising, and other private fundraising initiatives. The PDM serves as a trusted advisor and relationship builder, helping offices navigate growth opportunities while aligning local fundraising efforts with World Relief's broader mission and goals. Success in this role requires strong interpersonal skills, the ability to influence and coach diverse stakeholders, and a passion for developing teams as they expand their fundraising effectiveness. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who thrives at the intersection of relationship management, capacity building, strategic planning, and mission-driven leadership. 
 


ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strategic Planning & Implementation
- Partner with local office leadership to develop and implement integrated advancement strategies that strengthen church engagement, donor acquisition, donor retention, and private fundraising growth

- Facilitate strategic planning conversations with assigned offices to identify priorities, opportunities, and barriers to achieving annual fundraising and engagement goals
- Provide leadership to a portfolio of small and midsize offices, building strong relationships and serving as a trusted advisor to help offices navigate growth and change
 Capacity Building & Coaching
- Partner with office leadership teams to identify growth opportunities and provide targeted coaching to local leaders and development staff in fundraising best practices, equipping them to build healthy donor pipelines, deepen church and donor engagement, execute annual advancement plans, and achieve sustainable private revenue growth goa

About LawnStarter 
 LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings and two consecutive years of profitability. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services, and we're investing in the next generation of our platform to get there.
 About the Team 
 We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. We turn "I have a hunch" into "here's what actually happened," and we're the reason teams across the company can make calls on evidence instead of instinct. This role brings dedicated analytical firepower to the Pro (supply) side of that work.
 Requirements 
 The Role 
 As a Lead Product Data Analyst, you'll directly impact our results through insights and reports. You'll work closely with product managers, researchers, and other business stakeholders, helping with prioritization, assessments, and business recommendations. Alongside the rest of the Analytics team, it's your responsibility to nurture the data-driven culture within the company, making data easier to consume, whether through interactive reports, easy-to-use datasets, documentation, or training.
 You'll work with the autonomy of a Lead: setting your own standards, working independently, and acting as a trusted thought partner rather than an order-taker. That title isn't about managing people, there's no team attached to it. It's about the bar you hold your own analysis to, and the bar you help everyone around you reach.
 This role leans toward the Pro (supply) side of our marketplace, though the exact focus flexes with where the business needs the most insight.
 What You'll Own 
- Modeling & Analysis:  A marketplace is a complex system, with many moving parts and often contradicting signals. That creates an exciting pool of opportunities to find gaps, insights, and optimizations. Analyses range from a simple A/B test to a multivariate model on retention or ETA, backed by advanced SQL and intermediate Python or R.
- Reporting:  A complex system produces a high number of metrics worth tracking. A dashboard is only as good as our trust that it's correct and current. You'll understand the needs of the teams you work with and help create and maintain the reporting system, keeping it organized and easy to act on.
- Analytics Engineering:  Occasionally you'll work in the inner layers of the Data Warehouse to provide clean, documented datasets that power our reports and end users. We use dbt for transformation, so SQL is a must.
 Problems to Solve 
 Metrics nobody fully trusts.  Different teams cite different numbers for the same thing, and no one's quite sure which is current. Untangling that and giving the business one number it can stand behind is core to the job.
 Analysis that ships but doesn't move anything.  A technically correct answer that doesn't change a single decision is still a failure. Getting a stakeholder to actually act on what you found is the hard part, not the SQL.
 Data that's hard for anyone but an analyst to touch.  If every question requires filing a ticket and waiting on you, you haven't built a data-driven culture, you've built a bottleneck.
 A system with too many moving parts and not enough signal.  Supply, demand, pricing, and service quality all interact. Teasing out what's actually driving a metric versus what's noise is a real analytical problem, not a formality.
 What Success Looks Like (Year 1) 
- The metrics teams rely on daily are trusted, documented, and current, no one's quietly keeping a shadow spreadsheet because they don't trust the dashboard.
- Routine questions are self-serve: stakeholders find their own answers in existing reports instead of pinging you for a one-off pull.
- You can name specific decisions your analysis changed, not just analyses you delivered.
- The datasets and models you've built in dbt

About LawnStarter 
 LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.
 About the Data Team 
 We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.
 The Role 
 You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the  experimentation program : test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the  acquisition-to-conversion funnel  those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.
 You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.
 What makes this role different: 
- The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in.
- You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call.
 Requirements 
 What You'll Own 
- Experimentation rigor:  test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read.
- The self-serve experimentation layer:  automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve.
- The Growth funnel model:  a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment.
- The Growth analytics function model:  by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone.
 Problems to Solve 
 Tests that can't answer the question they were run for  Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

This role combines client engagement, solution design, and collaboration with internal teams to drive growth and enhance client experience.
 Key Responsibilities 
- Support development and presentation of treasury solutions for TPS clients.
- Assist with sales activities including proposals, pricing, and pipeline management.
- Analyze financial, company, and industry data to determine the needs of the client for proper structuring of the Bank's Treasury products and services
- Collaborate with Service and Onboarding teams to ensure smooth client implementation experience and service resolution.
- Maintain accurate records and reporting to track performance and client activity on Salesforce alongside aligned Treasury Consultant.
- Attends industry forums and community events, enhancing the Bank’s brand, staying updated on market trends, and leveraging insights to support sales strategies.
- Ensures adherence to regulatory requirements, internal controls, and compliance, mitigating risk and maintaining service standards.
 Qualifications 
- Bachelor’s degree required.
- 4–6 years of experience in banking, fintech, or corporate treasury.
- Strong analytical and data interpretation skills; proficiency with Excel and reporting tools.
- Advance level of knowledge of treasury products (e.g., liquidity management, payment solutions).
- Excellent communication and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple priorities.
